title: When love ends
hook: a breakup, a half-typed message, and an old line on hatred and love
tomorrow: an old list of how parents care for a child has no hugs in it. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Nakula's parents, who hoped to meet again in life after life: together. Today, the other side of that wish. What happens when together stops?

Late at night, a thumb hovers over a name. Block, or mute, or post the sad song everyone will understand. The breakup was weeks ago, and the group chat has opinions: never text back, never say their name, make sure they know what they lost. There's a message half-typed in the box, and it isn't kind. Here's the strange part. The person typing it once wished this other person well every single day, without trying. Where did that wish go? Did it have to end with everything else?
screen: `A THUMB OVER A NAME.` → `THE GROUP CHAT HAS OPINIONS.` → `A MESSAGE THAT ISN'T KIND.` → `WHERE DID THE WISH GO?`

segments.voice: Near its start, the Dhammapada has that exact message in someone's head: he abused me, he beat me, he robbed me. In those who keep turning thoughts like that over, the verse says, hatred never stops. Then a line Max Müller translated plainly: "For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule." Notice what it doesn't say. It doesn't say stay together, or stay friends, or pretend it didn't hurt. An ending can be right; sometimes leaving is the kindest thing two people do. What the verse watches is the wish underneath. Later, the teacher Buddhaghosa gave metta, loving-kindness, two enemies. The far enemy is ill will, easy to spot. The near enemy is greed, wanting, which can look exactly like love. A breakup is when you find out which one was there. If the wish for their good disappears the moment they stop being yours, it may have been wanting all along. If it can survive at a distance, that was metta. And if it's buried under hurt right now, it can take a while to come back. That's allowed. So kind at the end isn't staying. It's leaving without sending the cruel message. You can mute them, keep your distance, grieve hard, and still not wish them harm. The relationship ends. The wish for their good doesn't have to.
screen: `HE ABUSED ME, HE ROBBED ME.` · `HATRED CEASES BY LOVE.` · `THE NEAR ENEMY LOOKS LIKE LOVE.` · `DISTANCE, WITHOUT HARM.` · then, large: `KIND AT THE END.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone from your past: a former partner, or a friend you drifted from. Choose someone it feels safe to think about, and skip anyone who harmed you, for now. From wherever you are, wish them one plain thing: may you be well. You don't have to want them back to mean it.
When love ends: the moment metta gets tested. The bond can stop, and the wish for someone's good can stay.
Hold on to this: kind at the end, even from far away. Seven of eleven on family.

howItsDone: Buddhists practice metta, wishing beings well, at home and in temples; some teachers suggest bringing a former partner or a difficult person into that practice only once it feels safe.

fork.setup: your ex is seated at the next table at your cousin's wedding. what does kind at the end look like here?
options: go over and reconnect; real metta means getting close again.
be polite, keep your distance, and quietly wish them well.
leave early so you never have to deal with them at all.
fork.reveal: the verse asks for no hatred, not for closeness. distance is allowed; ill will is what the teaching sets down.

original.note: Pali: loving-kindness, the wish that beings be well and happy.

chat.says: ava and jake broke up. she wants me to unfollow him and hate him forever. do i have to?
options: Unfollow if it helps her. But you can keep your distance without wishing him harm.
Hate him a little. Loving-kindness is for strangers, not people who hurt your friend.
Stay friends with him like nothing happened; being kind means never picking a side.
chat.meaning: Hatred doesn't end by hatred. Distance is fine; kind at the end means not wishing the other person harm.

tie.story: The Dhammapada says hatred never ends by hatred, only by love, and Buddhaghosa warned that wanting can pass for love.
tie.friend: Mai can stand with Ava and even mute Jake, without wishing him harm.
tie.you: is there someone from your past you could wish well, from a distance?
